To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel bacterial platform to produce a variety of bioactive proteins, with titers up to 400-fold higher than wild type levels, and with minimal truncation, aggregation, or other contaminants common in cytosolic expression systems.

we have developed a bacterial platform for the production of high titer secreted proteins, including those with challenging biochemistries, and have demonstrated the utility of the system for a variety of proteins.
we engineered the T3SS to secrete proteins in high titer and high purity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the engineering of the T3SS to create an efficient and versatile secretion system for the production of heterologous proteins. 1
developing the tools to enable the production of proteins in bacteria that are difficult or impossible to produce in other systems.
the engineering of the type III secretion system in bacteria to enable high titer production and secretion of a variety of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T3SS is an ideal secretion system for heterologous protein production in bacteria.
the T3SS is a powerful and flexible platform for the production of proteins that are difficult to produce using other methods, and that the engineering steps are relatively straightforward.

we have engineered a bacterial secretion system that enables efficient production of biochemically difficult proteins in a single step process, with minimal purification requirements and at high titer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the T3SS platform can be engineered to secrete any heterologous protein at titers comparable to cytosolic production, while maintaining the advantages of secretion, and without the need for expensive and time consuming downstream processing.

we have engineered a bacterial protein secretion system to be the equivalent of a eukaryotic secretion system, but with the advantages of bacterial expression, including high cell density, low cost, rapid scale-up, and ease of purification.

the engineering of the T3SS has enabled the production of a wide variety of proteins that are otherwise challenging to produce, including those that are toxic to the cell and/or difficult to fold into functional forms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a bacterial T3SS is a viable alternative to eukaryotic secretion platforms, with the potential to enable the production of a wide variety of proteins at a fraction of the cost and effort of current production methods.
the T3SS is a versatile platform for the secretion of a variety of heterologous proteins.
it is possible to engineer a bacterial secretion system to produce high quality heterologous proteins at titers comparable to those of the best eukaryotic expression systems.
